form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Johnson (for himself and Mr. Peters) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

form.official-title: To eliminate or modify certain Federal agency reporting requirements, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Congressional Reporting Burden Reduction Act.

section.header: Elimination of Department of Homeland Security reports

subsection.header: Consolidation of reports on antidumping and countervailing duties
subsection.text: Section 691(a) of the North American Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act (19 U.S.C. 1671l) is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking the subsection heading and inserting the following: Report on antidumping and countervailing duty collections and other related matters;
by striking The and inserting the following: (1) In general.—Not later than April 30 each year, the;
in paragraph (1), as designated by paragraph (2) of this section—

subparagraph.text: by striking before the 60th day of each fiscal year after fiscal year 1994; and
by striking preceding fiscal year and inserting most recently completed fiscal year; and

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.text: If the Commissioner prepares a report described in subparagraph (B) for a fiscal year, the Commissioner shall submit any such report with the report required under paragraph (1) for that year.
The reports described in this subparagraph are the following reports specified in Senate Report 114–264 (2017), accompanying S. 3001, 114th Congress:

clause.text: AD/CVD Collection New Shipper Single Entry Bonds.

subsection.text: Paragraph (2) under the heading Disaster relief fund (including transfer of funds) under the heading Federal Emergency Management Agency in title I of the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2015 (Public Law 114–4; 129 Stat. 55) is amended, in the matter preceding subparagraph (A), by striking fifth day of each month and inserting fifth business day of each month.

subsection.header: Department of Homeland Security collection of conference fees report
subsection.text: Section 554 of the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2010 (6 U.S.C. 469a) is amended by striking : Provided further and all that follows through prior fiscal year.

Title III of division F of the joint explanatory statement of the committee of conference accompanying the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2017 (Public Law 115–31) is amended, under the heading Federal Protection Service under the heading National Protection and Programs Directorate, by striking The Secretary and the Director of OMB shall certify in writing to the Committees, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, that FPS operations will be fully funded in fiscal year 2017 through the collection of security fees. Should sufficient revenue not be collected to fully fund operations, an expenditure plan is required describing how security risks will be adequately addressed..

subsection.header: Under Secretary for Management quarterly staffing requirement
subsection.text: Title I of division F of the joint explanatory statement of the committee of conference accompanying the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2017 (Public Law 115–31) is amended, under the heading Office of the Chief Financial Officer under the heading Office of the Secretary and Executive Management under the heading Departmental Management, Operations, Intelligence, and Oversight, by striking the following: The Department shall continue submitting obligation plans to the Committees on a quarterly basis, with the first plan due with-in 45 days of enactment of this Act. These plans shall be consistent with direction provided in the explanatory statement accompanying Public Law 114–113, which required comparisons of planned and actual obligations, by PPA, of all salaries and benefits funding..

subsection.text: Section 515(b) of the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2005 (Public Law 108–334; 49 U.S.C. 44945 note) is repealed.
Section 286(t) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1356(t)) is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking paragraph (2); and
by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2).

subparagraph.text: As part of each report submitted under paragraph (1)(C), the Administrator shall conduct an investigation of the cost of travel and the operation of privately owned airplanes and privately owned motorcycles by employees while engaged on official business.
In conducting each investigation required under subparagraph (A), the Administrator shall review and analyze, among other factors—

subsection.text: Chapter 11 of title 31, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: in section 1105(a), by striking paragraph (39); and
in section 1125—

clause.text: by striking Annually and inserting On a biennial basis; and
in paragraph (4), by inserting , who shall submit to Congress that total count and list before the period at the end; and

by striking In addition to including the list of plans and reports determined to be outdated or duplicative by each agency in the budget of the United States Government, as provided by section 1105(a)(37), 1 the and inserting The;
inserting with the submission under subsection (a)(4) after concurrently; and
by striking such plans and reports and inserting plans and reports determined to be outdated or duplicative by each agency.

section.text: Notwithstanding Senate Report 114–280 and House Report 114–624, beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, the Office of Management and Budget shall—

paragraph.text: provide annual, and not quarterly, reports to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on the savings of the program; and

report to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on an annual, and not quarterly, basis on the status of the 10 highest priority information technology investment projects.
